correctness.rationale: Any factorization psi2 o psi1 with composite phi(b)=b and nonempty images forces psi1(b) to be one letter; a possible intermediate swap normalizes both factors to fix b. Their images of a contain a, so their a-counts multiply m=cd. For boundary-free w, nonunit factors force c,d>=2; exact substitution v[u] reproduces precisely the same c-1 internal gaps in every c-a block, with between-block gaps free. The converse constructs both nonunit factors. Endpoint padding yields the separate reducible case and for m=1 two nonunits require two b symbols. The m=4 count and fixed-composite-m asymptotic follow from integer-composition generating functions. Independently brute-enumerated all normalized nonunit factor pairs for 502 words of lengths 1..8 and matched the criterion; finite verification corroborates but cannot prove the universal iff.

originality.rationale: The closest Bell--Foster--Reidenbach arXiv full HTML explicitly has general factor-basis criterion Theorem 1 but Proposition 18(ii) asserts every upper-triangular incidence matrix with beta=1, alpha>=2 gives reducible morphism. Word aba fixing b has two a symbols with no nontrivial multiplicative split and is irreducible, whereas aab with same incidence matrix has boundary b and factors. The source theorem does not give the all-word periodic gap iff and its stated matrix implication is actually false. Resultary returned synchronization/rank-compression records, not this composition criterion. Prior combinatorics-on-words literature under other factorization terminology remains an originality risk.

value.rationale: Provides an exact constructive decision law for a natural infinite family of binary endomorphisms and pinpoints a false matrix-only assertion in the paper motivating the question. Word-order sensitivity, prime-case counts and sparse reducibility among composite fixed-m boundary-free words are mathematically meaningful consequences, not a trivial new name or small brute-force slice.

final_claim: For rank-preserving free-semigroup endomorphisms phi(a)=w containing a and phi(b)=b, the exact reducibility criterion is endpoint b-padding (for m>=2) or a repeated interior b-gap block indexed by a proper divisor c of m=|w|_a; for m=1 reducible iff at least two b letters. Boundary-free prime-m words are irreducible; phi(a)=aba refutes the matrix-level exclusive reducibility assertion of Bell--Foster--Reidenbach Prop.18(ii).
